# 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK Mattress Removal Cost: What You Will Actually Pay  

**A single mattress removal from 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK typically costs between **$70 and $100**.** That range is the company’s published single‑item price for mattresses, before any state‑mandated recycling fee (e.g., $10.50 in California, Connecticut, Rhode Island).  

Below is everything you need to know about how that price is calculated, when it makes sense to add a mattress to a larger load, how to prepare the item, and what cheaper alternatives exist.

---

## How 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK Prices Mattress Removal  

### Single‑Item vs. Volume Load  

- **Single‑item pricing**: $70‑$100 per mattress. This is the base rate you’ll see on the on‑site estimate if the crew is only hauling the mattress.  
- **Volume‑based pricing**: The company charges by the fraction of a truck you occupy. A **minimum load (1/8‑truck)** runs **$100‑$150**, which can be cheaper per item if you have several pieces.  
- **Half‑truck** (5 ft × 5 ft × 8 ft) is **$400‑$600**; a **full‑truck** (10 ft × 5 ft × 8 ft, ~18 cu yd) is **$600‑$1,000**.  

If you only need a mattress removed, the single‑item price is the most transparent. If you have other junk (couches, appliances, boxes), grouping them into a volume load often reduces the per‑item cost.

### What’s Included in the Price  

- **All labor** – crew members load the mattress from wherever it sits on your property (no curb‑side requirement).  
- **Hauling and disposal** – transport to an authorized landfill or recycling center.  
- **Recycling fees** – any state‑mandated fees (e.g., $10.50 for mattress recycling in CA, CT, RI) are passed through.  
- **Cleanup** – the crew sweeps the area after loading.  
- **Licensing & insurance** – you’re covered if anything goes wrong during the pickup.  

No hidden fuel surcharges or “dump fees” appear after the crew arrives.

---

## Real‑World Cost Scenarios  

### Solo Mattress Pickup  

| Item | Base price | State recycling fee (if applicable) | Total |
|------|------------|--------------------------------------|-------|
| Mattress (single) | **$70‑$100** | **$0‑$10.50** (CA/CT/RI) | **$70‑$110.50** |

If you live in a state without the Bye‑Bye‑Mattress program, you’ll pay the lower end of the range. In California, expect the top of the range plus $10.50.

### Adding a Mattress to a Larger Load – Worked Example  

Suppose you have:

- 1 mattress ($90 average)  
- 1 sofa ($150 average)  
- 30 cu ft of mixed junk (≈ 0.1 truck)

**Step 1 – Estimate volume**  
A half‑truck is 5 ft × 5 ft × 8 ft = 200 cu ft. Your items occupy roughly 0.15 of a half‑truck, well within the **minimum 1/8‑truck** bracket.

**Step 2 – Compare pricing**  

| Option | Calculation | Cost |
|--------|-------------|------|
| Single‑item mattress only | $90 + $0 (no fee) | **$90** |
| Single‑item sofa only | $150 | **$150** |
| Combined volume (1/8‑truck) | $100‑$150 (minimum load) | **$100‑$150** |

**Result:** By bundling the mattress and sofa into a single 1/8‑truck load, you pay **$100‑$150** total, which is **$40‑$110** cheaper than hiring two separate single‑item pickups.

**Bottom line:** Whenever you have more than one bulky item, ask the crew for a volume quote; the per‑item cost will almost always drop.

---

## Preparing Your Mattress for Removal  

### How to Measure and Stage  

1. **Measure the mattress** (length × width × height). Most standard mattresses (twin, queen, king) fit comfortably within the 1/8‑truck dimensions (1.25 ft × 5 ft × 8 ft).  
2. **Clear a pathway** from the mattress to the loading zone. Remove rugs, breakable items, and ensure doors are wide enough.  
3. **If possible, strip the bedding** (sheets, box spring) to reduce weight and volume.  

### What the Crew Will Do  

- **Lift and protect** the mattress with a blanket or tarp.  
- **Load it onto the truck** using a hand‑truck or dolly; no need for you to carry it.  
- **Inspect for hazardous materials** (e.g., foam with fire retardants) – they handle disposal according to local regulations.  

---

## Alternatives to Paying 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK  

| Option | Typical Cost | Pros | Cons |
|--------|--------------|------|------|
| **Municipal bulky‑item pickup** | Free to $30 (varies by city) | No private‑company fee; often scheduled monthly | Limited to one item per household; strict size limits; may require you to bring item to curb |
| **Retailer haul‑away** (e.g., IKEA, Mattress Firm) | Free with purchase or $20‑$40 for old item | Convenient; often coordinated with delivery | Only works when you buy a new item; may not accept damaged mattresses |
| **Donation** (Goodwill, Habitat for Humanity) | Free (tax‑deductible receipt) | Good for charity; saves landfill space | Must be in decent condition; you must transport to drop‑off |
| **DIY dumpster rental** (1‑day roll‑off) | $250‑$400 for 10‑cu‑yd (depends on city) | Handles unlimited items; you control timing | Requires you to load and dispose; may exceed local landfill fees |
| **LoadUp (online, per‑item)** | $89 minimum; mattress $70‑$100 | Guaranteed price online; often 20‑30 % cheaper | Not available in every state; may add a $25‑$30 service fee |

#### When a Cheaper Alternative Beats 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK  

- **You have a single, clean mattress and live in a city with free bulky‑item pickup.** Call your local waste department first.  
- **You’re buying a new mattress** and the retailer offers free haul‑away.  
- **Your mattress is still in good condition** and you can transport it a short distance; donation saves you money and earns a tax receipt.  
- **You have many items** (furniture, construction debris, yard waste) and a roll‑off dumpster fits the volume better than a truck‑based service.

## Common Mistakes & What People Get Wrong  

| Mistake | Why It Happens | How to Avoid It |
|---------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Assuming the quoted $70‑$100 includes the recycling fee.** | The fee is state‑specific and added at the end of the job. | Ask the crew if your state has a mattress‑recycling mandate before the estimate. |
| **Calling “discount codes” found on coupon sites.** | Most codes are outdated or never verified by the franchise. | Sign up for the company’s email list for the only reliable $10‑$25 off offers. |
| **Scheduling a curb‑side pickup when the crew can load from inside.** | Some customers think they must move the mattress to the curb to avoid extra fees. | Remember the price includes **loading from anywhere on your property** – no extra charge. |
| **Booking a separate truck for each item.** | Misunderstanding that each item gets its own truck. | Combine items into the smallest possible volume load; the minimum 1/8‑truck is often cheaper than two single‑item jobs. |
| **Skipping the on‑site estimate.** | Trying to get a quick price online or over the phone. | 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK only provides a free, no‑obligation on‑site estimate; that’s the only accurate figure. |

---

## Frequently Asked Questions  

**1. Do I have to pay a deposit or give a credit card when I book?**  
No. The on‑site estimate is free and does not require a credit card. You only pay after the crew completes the job.

**2. How far in advance should I schedule a mattress pickup?**  
Same‑day service is often available, but booking 24‑48 hours ahead gives the crew flexibility and may improve scheduling options.

**3. What if my mattress is broken or has a strong odor?**  
The crew handles all conditions; there is no extra charge for damage or odor. They are trained to dispose of hazardous foam safely.

**4. Can I split the cost with a neighbor?**  
Yes. If you share a truck load, the total charge is divided among the parties. This is a proven way to lower the per‑item price.

**5. Are there any hidden fees for stairs or long walks?**  
No. The quoted price includes loading from anywhere on the property, even up multiple flights of stairs. Any extra work beyond standard loading (e.g., dismantling a built‑in) would be discussed beforehand.

**6. What happens to the mattress after it’s hauled away?**  
In most states the mattress is taken to a recycling facility. In California, Connecticut, and Rhode Island a **$10.50 per‑unit recycling fee** is applied under the Bye‑Bye‑Mattress program.

---

## Bottom‑Line Takeaway  

- **A single mattress removal by 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK costs $70‑$100** (plus a possible $10.50 recycling fee in three states).  
- **If you have other bulky items, request a volume quote**; a minimum 1/8‑truck load ($100‑$150) usually beats two separate single‑item pickups.  
- **Prepare the mattress** by clearing a path and removing bedding; the crew does all the heavy lifting.  
- **Consider free municipal pickup, retailer haul‑away, donation, or a DIY dumpster** before paying the private‑company rate—especially if you live in a city with a free bulky‑item program.  
- **Discounts are limited** to email‑list offers and local franchise promotions; coupon sites are largely unreliable.  

By understanding the pricing structure and comparing alternatives, you can decide whether 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK is the right solution for your mattress removal or if a cheaper, community‑based option makes more sense.
